title: SGB bought on the exchange, redeemed by RBI on maturity in Nov-2026 (tax year 2026-27): not exempt for a secondary buyer under the Finance Act 2026 position; LT 12.5 %, no Rs 1.25 lakh exemption
rules: Position adopted per brief (UNVERIFIED): from 1-Apr-2026 (Finance Act 2026 / Income-tax Act 2025 (in force from 1-Apr-2026; tax year 2026-27)) redemption of an SGB is not a transfer only for an individual who subscribed at the original issue and held it continuously until redemption on maturity; any other redemption is a transfer of a listed security
Redemption is an extinguishment of rights -> transfer (Income-tax Act 1961 s.2(47)(ii) and its counterpart in the 2025 Act)

Holding period: listed security -> long-term if held more than 12 months (1961 Act s.2(42A) first proviso as amended by Finance (No.2) Act 2024; carried into the 2025 Act - section number not verified)
Rate: 12.5 % without indexation on LTCG of a non-s.112A asset (1961 Act s.112(1) as amended by Finance (No.2) Act 2024; believed to be s.197 of the 2025 Act - unverified)
s.112A exemption of Rs 1.25 lakh applies only to STT-paid equity shares / equity-oriented fund units / business-trust units -> not to SGB
derivation: Buy on exchange 2021-03-10: 10 @ 4,500.00 -> cost 45,000.00 (not an original subscriber).
RBI redemption on maturity 2026-11-20: 10 @ 12,500.00 -> proceeds 1,25,000.00. Transfer after 31-Mar-2026 -> Income-tax Act 2025, tax year 2026-27 (fy 2027).
Holder is not an original subscriber -> the (assumed) Finance Act 2026 condition fails -> redemption is a transfer of a listed security.
fy 2027: tax 80,000 x 0.125 = 10,000.00; cess 400.00; total 10,400.00; exemption_used 0.00 (not a s.112A asset).
Had the 1961 Act s.47(viic) wording continued (any redemption by an individual), the answer would be exempt with exempt_total 80,000.00 and tax 0.00.
